A marker stays where it was: "Removed where the law requires, {date}, by {member}". Published cases are not changed; a court order for those is complied with on the docket.

rewrite.screen.places.wanted.help: Kept in your group's Civicsmith and never sent anywhere. When an update brings its rules and offices, administrators are told once in their queue and can choose it above.
rewrite.screen.proceeding.login.note: The court's register needs a login, so new filings come only by a member's own capture.
rewrite.screen.projectai.account.suspended: Your sign-in no longer serves {project}. A second member joined, and a sign-in serves a project only while it has one member. Members' acts here now use their own accounts, or the group's key. Add an API key to give the project its own account again; if the project returns to just you, your sign-in serves it again.
rewrite.screen.projectai.notice.head: Before your first question here
rewrite.screen.recovery.held: You hold recovery codes: {remaining} of {total} unused, issued {date}.
rewrite.screen.recovery.shown: Save these now: they are shown only this once. Keep them somewhere only you can reach, apart from your password. Civicsmith keeps only a fingerprint of each, so it can never show them again.
rewrite.screen.reset.keeps: Your handle and everything you did stay as they are, and every other sign-in of yours ends. {name} can't see the password you choose. Your recovery codes still work; if you have lost them too, get ten new ones in Settings › Recovery codes once you are in.
rewrite.screen.reset.dead.what: It was used already, it expired, or an administrator withdrew it. Ask an administrator for a new one, in person or however your group talks. Nothing was changed.
rewrite.screen.review-copy.heading: Share Edition {edition} for review
rewrite.screen.review-outside.heading: A review copy from {group}
rewrite.screen.request.describe: Describe the records, not why you want them. The law doesn't let the office limit access because of why you ask ({cite}), and the city's portal shows this text to anyone.
rewrite.screen.request.howsend.1: Open the city's public records portal ({portal}) and choose “{button}”.
rewrite.screen.request.howsend.2: Paste the approved text as the request description, and choose the department: {department}.
rewrite.screen.request.howsend.3: Contact details are optional. Without them the request still goes in, but the city can't send you updates or ask you to clarify, and you can't sign in to collect the records. Give the address your group uses for its requests; staff see what you give.
rewrite.screen.standard.notyet: Not a standard until a member adopts it.
rewrite.screen.ties.says.name.choice: Naming me by my handle: “{handle}, who worked on this case, is {tie}.”
rewrite.screen.ties.says.group.choice: Without naming me: “A member of the group who worked on this case is {tie}.”
rewrite.screen.timeline.order.evidence: More evidence could order them: a passage that gives either one its day (a ledger entry, a meeting's agenda, a letter's date), or a source that says which came first. Until a source orders them, both are kept as they are, never guessed into order; when one does, the timeline names it, and a source that disagrees is shown beside it, in tension.
rewrite.shell.unavailable.nothing.says: This address doesn't lead to anything in your group's Civicsmith. It may have been typed wrong, or the link is old.
rewrite.shell.unavailable.notyours.says: It exists, or it may not: either way it isn't something you can see. A hidden project shows only to its own members; ask its owner if you think you should be in it.
rewrite.shell.unavailable.unreachable.title: Your group's Civicsmith can't be reached
rewrite.shell.unavailable.unreachable.says: Your device is offline, or your group's Civicsmith isn't answering. Nothing you did is lost: what you saved is kept there, and what you were typing is still on this page.
rewrite.screen.wizards.copy.note: A copy becomes your group's own wizard: a draft until approved, like any wizard your group writes. The original stays as it is and is still offered; a required wizard stays required. The copy shows what it is based on, and when Civicsmith's original changes, your wizard editors are told and can bring the change across.
rewrite.screen.setup.name: Set up your group's Civicsmith
rewrite.screen.setup.lede: Welcome. Civicsmith is installed and waiting for you. First, claim it, so that only you can run it; it takes about two minutes. Then tell it a little about your group. Only the claim is needed today: every other part starts with a safe choice, and you can change any of it later in Settings.
rewrite.screen.setup.otp.help: Already filled in if you came straight from the installer.
rewrite.screen.setup.handle.help: The name you sign in with, shown on your work and on every case you sign. Choose it with care: it can't be changed later.
rewrite.screen.setup.own.help: At least 12 characters. From now on you sign in with your handle and this password.
rewrite.screen.setup.name.help: Shown at the top of every page, on invitations and on everything your group publishes. You can change it any time.
rewrite.screen.setup.name.now: Saved. Your group is now called {name}.
rewrite.screen.setup.domain.help: Civicsmith gives you one small file to put on your website. Once it's there, anyone reading what your group publishes can check that it really comes from you. Whoever looks after your website can do this in a few minutes.
rewrite.screen.setup.places.help: Not listed? Choose “Somewhere else”. Everything still works; you enter deadlines and offices yourself.
rewrite.screen.setup.places.chosen: You chose {place} when you installed. Change it if you need to.
rewrite.screen.setup.place.wanted.help: When an update brings its rules, Civicsmith tells you, and you can switch to it here. What you type stays in your group's Civicsmith and is never sent anywhere.
rewrite.screen.setup.offices.what: Civicsmith can fill in the public offices of {place}, and who holds each one today, from the place's own records. Check the list, then confirm it. You can add others at any time.
rewrite.screen.setup.offices.none: Civicsmith doesn't know the offices of {place} yet, so this list starts empty. Add the offices your group deals with, now or whenever they come up. When an update brings their rules, you'll be told, and the offices you added stay.
rewrite.screen.setup.office.note: Anything your group should know about it (optional)
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.what: Civicsmith can include an AI assistant, built on Anthropic's Claude. Members ask it, in everyday words, to find, read and check things in your group's material. It works only from what your group holds, gives legal information but never legal advice, and never decides, signs or sends anything. Everything in Civicsmith also works without it.
rewrite.screen.setup.keepaway: No, keep our material away from AI
rewrite.screen.setup.keepaway.help: Required. Every member will see it.
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.own: A member who wants the assistant connects their own Claude subscription or API key. It serves only them, at their own cost, and costs your group nothing.
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.paid: One Anthropic API key, paid for by your group, serves every member who has no account of their own. A member's own account still comes first.
rewrite.screen.setup.key.help: Made in Anthropic's Console, under an account your group pays for. Civicsmith locks it away and never shows it again.
rewrite.screen.setup.limit: The most each member may use per day
rewrite.screen.setup.limit.help: Applies only to your group's key, never to a member's own account. More limits are in Settings › Members.
rewrite.screen.setup.people.what: Facts about a person that come from public documents are as visible as those documents are. Your group's own notes about a person stay inside the project where they were written.
rewrite.screen.setup.court.what: Civicsmith keeps your group's unpublished work private, from the public and from the people you look into. But a court order your group can't defeat can still require anything not public to be shown, such as members' notes, sources and hidden projects. Much work never draws such an order, and journalists, lawyers and auditors may have protections others lack.
rewrite.screen.setup.court.legend: Should members be told about this?
rewrite.screen.setup.court.tell: Yes, when they join, and the first time they save something not public
rewrite.screen.setup.court.dont: No, just keep the explanation one tap away
rewrite.screen.setup.admins.what: Right now you're the only administrator. If you're away or lose access, no one else can run your group's Civicsmith. Invite someone you trust as a second administrator, now or later.
rewrite.screen.setup.security.scanner: Civicsmith's own file scanner checks every file your group brings in, and risky ones open in a safe view. You don't need to do anything.
rewrite.screen.setup.security.what: If your organization already uses its own file scanner, a tool that makes safe copies of files, or a log service, you can connect it here or later in Settings › Security.
rewrite.screen.setup.finished.what: Anything you left is waiting in Settings. Next, invite your first members.
